chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If there remains on him (the husband) something of the dowry (mahr) and he knows that she has a husband, then whatever she took is hers for what she made permissible of her private part (consummation), and he retains for her what remains with him.

And whenever a man releases the woman before he enters with her in the 'mut'ah (temporary marriage), and he had given her the dowry, it becomes obligatory upon her to return half of what she took from him.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for returning half the dowry in temporary marriage before consummation?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the financial rights in temporary marriage (*mut'ah*) by distinguishing between partial and full dowry settlements upon dissolution before consummation. It establishes that if the husband retains the wife's exclusivity (*istihlal*) while owing part of the mahr, she keeps what she received and he keeps the rest; conversely, if the full mahr was paid, she returns half, reflecting the principle of proportional compensation for the period of validity.
